questions.q: Distinguish between concave and convex mirrors, and give their uses.
answer: Spherical mirrors are of two kinds, differing in the way their surfaces curve and in the images they form.

answer.text: Its reflecting surface curves inward and it converges light. It can form real or virtual, magnified images and is used in shaving and dentists' mirrors, in torch and headlight reflectors, and in solar cookers.
Its reflecting surface curves outward and it diverges light. It always forms a small, virtual, erect image and gives a wide field of view, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles.

answer: Both obey the laws of reflection, and their different curvatures decide the images they produce.

questions.q: Distinguish between convex and concave lenses and state their uses.

answer.text: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges the light passing through it. It can form real or virtual images and is used as a magnifying glass, in cameras, and in spectacles to correct long sight, or hypermetropia. Focused sunlight from a convex lens can even burn paper.
A concave lens is thinner in the middle and diverges light. It always forms a small, virtual, erect image and is used in spectacles to correct short sight, or myopia.
Thus a convex lens converges light and magnifies, while a concave lens diverges light and reduces, each with its own everyday uses.

questions.q: How does a plane mirror form an image, and what are the characteristics of that image?

answer.text: forms an image by reflecting light according to the laws of reflection — the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

list: It is virtual (cannot be caught on a screen) and erect (upright)
It is the same size as the object
It is formed as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
It is laterally inverted — the left and right sides appear interchanged

answer.text: is why the word AMBULANCE is written reversed on vehicles so it reads correctly in a driver's mirror.

questions.q: How is white light dispersed into colours, and what does this tell us about sunlight?

answer.text: is the splitting of white light into its component colours when it passes through a prism.

list: A glass prism bends different colours by different amounts, spreading them into a band of seven colours — the spectrum
The order is violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red

answer.text: that white light, such as sunlight, is not a single colour but a mixture of seven colours.

list: A rainbow forms when raindrops act like tiny prisms and disperse sunlight
Recombining the seven colours gives back white light
